title: Chapter 21. Appendix. Padas signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini — V: the wedding with Lakshmipriya and the beginning of the second wedding
html:
Continuation of the appendix (the introductory note on the two Naraharis, on the arguments for attribution and on the marks in the headings is in ch. 17). Chapter 21: the end of GPT section 2.3 "Karnavedha and the wedding" — the wedding day with Lakshmipriya (the morning after the adhivasa, the water rite, the bath and dressing of the bridegroom, the procession, the wedding in the house of Vallabha Acharya, the bridal chamber, the return home) and life with Lakshmipriya; the beginning of section 2.4 "The second marriage" — the news of the wedding with Vishnupriya, the women of Nadia with Shachi, the adhivasa of bridegroom and bride, the morning of the wedding day (the bath and dressing of the bridegroom; the procession and the wedding itself follow in the next chapter). Narahari Chakravarti quotes almost all the padas of the chapter one after another in the 12th wave of the Bhakti-ratnakara, where Ishana shows Srinivasa the house of Jagannatha Mishra (two padas of section 2.4 are also in Chakravarti's Gaura-charita-chintamani); one (no. 13) has not been found in any witness. Before translation the "Narahari" signatures in sections 2.3–2.4 (GPT1 pp. 84–100) were checked throughout, in the OCR and on the scan: the catalogue had missed two padas of section 2.4 (nos. 18 and 23, new rows NG-285, 286). From section 2.4, up to the adhivasa and the morning of the wedding, the following are not translated: nos. 4 and 11 — signed Ghanashyama (outside the appendix); nos. 2, 3 and 7 — padas in nagari-bhava (a young wife's dream in which Gaura invites her to the wedding and embraces her; the "anuraga" of the women for Gaura; women who give Him "life and youth") — assigned to the section of nagari padas. The base text is GPT1 (doubtful places from the scan), collated with GPT2, the BR (eds. 1912 and 1960) and the Gaura-charita-chintamani (ed. 1947); PK, KGC, PS and the Gita-chandrodaya have been checked. On Lakshmipriya and Vishnupriya as the eternal energies of the Lord and on the wedding rites as lila see notes 2 and 30; on the motif of the women of Nadia, note 5. The notes of the GPT editors are not reproduced.

1. Narahari — "adhibāsa niśi pohāile…" (GPT1 p. 85, section 2.3, no. 16; BR)

The wedding day: the night of the adhivasa is over; Nimai, surrounded by brahmanas, performs the Vedic rites; crowds, music, songs, the praises of the bhatas, the women's cries of joy; everyone rejoices at the women's rites. Raga kamoda. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the BR (12th wave).1

অধিবাস নিশি পোহাইলে । বিবাহের কার্য্য যত করয়ে সকলে ॥

adhibāsa niśi pohāile | bibāhera kāryya yata karaye sakale ||

adhibāsa niśi pohāile — when the night of the adhivasa had passed; bibāhera kāryya yata — all the wedding tasks; karaye sakale — everyone performs

1.1When the night of the adhivasa had passed, everyone set about the wedding tasks.

বিপ্রগণে হইয়া বেষ্টিত । নিমাই করেন ক্রিয়া যে বেদবিহিত ॥

bipragaṇe haiyā beṣṭita | nimāi karena kriyā ye bedabihita ||

bipragaṇe haiyā beṣṭita — surrounded by brahmanas; nimāi karena kriyā — Nimai performs the rites; ye beda-bihita — which are enjoined by the Vedas

1.2Surrounded by brahmanas, Nimai performs the rites enjoined by the Vedas.2

লোক ভীড় কহিলে না হয় । লেহ দেহ বাক্য কোলাহল অতিশয় ॥

loka bhīṛa kahile nā haya | leha deha bākya kolāhala atiśaya ||

loka bhīṛa — the crowd of people; kahile nā haya — cannot be told; leha deha bākya — the cries "take! give!"; kolāhala atiśaya — the clamour is immense

1.3The crowds cannot be described: the clamour of "take! give!" is immense.

বাজে নানা বাদ্য নিরন্তর । গায়কগণেতে গান করে পূর্ব্বাপর ॥

bāje nānā bādya nirantara | gāyakagaṇete gāna kare pūrvvāpara ||

bāje nānā bādya nirantara — instruments of every kind play without pause; gāyaka-gaṇete gāna kare — the singers sing; pūrvvāpara — one [song] after another

1.4Instruments of every kind play without pause; the singers sing song after song.

ভাটগণে পড়ে কায়বার । নারীগণে দেই সুমধুর যজকার ॥

bhāṭagaṇe paṛe kāyabāra | nārīgaṇe dei sumadhura yajakāra ||

bhāṭa-gaṇe paṛe kāyabāra — the bhatas recite verses of praise; nārī-gaṇe dei — the women raise; sumadhura yajakāra — sweet cries of joy

1.5The bhatas recite verses of praise; the women raise sweet cries of joy.

সবার উল্লাস স্ত্রী-আচারে । নরহরি ভাসে সেনা সুখের সায়রে ॥

sabāra ullāsa strī-ācāre | narahari bhāse senā sukhera sāyare ||

sabāra ullāsa — all rejoice; strī-ācāre — at the women's rites; narahari bhāse — Narahari floats; senā sukhera sāyare — in that ocean of happiness

1.6All rejoice at the women's rites; Narahari floats in that ocean of happiness.3

BR — 12th wave (ed. 1912, pp. 790–791; ed. 1960, vv. 1277–1282), straight after the adhivasa of the bride (no. 22 of chapter 20); then the BR gives the padas nos. 2–12 of this chapter in sequence. Variants: 1.4 GPT1 "pūrvvāpara" ("one after another"), BR "manohara" ("enchantingly"); 1.6 GPT1 "sāyare", BR "pāthāre" (both "in the ocean"). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. The wedding with Lakshmipriya — CB Adi 10; CC Adi 15; Murari 1.9–1.10. lila with His own energy. The Lord, the goal of all the Vedas, is bound by nothing enjoined; He accepts the wedding rites in keeping with the lila and for the joy of His mother and His associates — as Krishna did in Dvaraka. So are all the padas of this chapter on the Lord's "marriage" to be understood. water rite, the anointing of the bridegroom, etc.). Here too the poet places himself in the lila as a witness and participant (cf. note 24 of chapter 20).

2. Narahari — "kulabadhūgaṇa ulasita mana…" (GPT1 p. 85, no. 17; BR)

The wives of noble families dress to go for the water of the wedding bath; looking at Gora's face, they cry "ulu-lu"; they go, talking among themselves; anklets ring, music plays; having performed the water rite, they enter the house. Raga kamoda. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the BR.4

কুলবধূগণ উলসিত মন পানি-সহিবারে সাজয়ে রঙ্গে ।
গোরা-মুখশশী হেরি হেরি হাসি উলু লুলু দেই পুলক অঙ্গে ॥

kulabadhūgaṇa ulasita mana pāni-sahibāre sājaye raṅge |
gorā-mukhaśaśī heri heri hāsi ulu lulu dei pulaka aṅge ||

kulabadhū-gaṇa — the wives of noble families; ulasita mana — their hearts rejoicing; pāni-sahibāre — for the water [rite]; sājaye raṅge — gaily dress; gorā-mukha-śaśī — Gora's moonlike face; heri heri — gazing again and again; hāsi — smiling; ulu lulu dei — cry "ulu-lu"; pulaka aṅge — a thrill in the body

2.1The wives of noble families, their hearts rejoicing, gaily dress to go for the water; gazing again and again at Gora's moonlike face, they smile and cry "ulu-lu", and a thrill runs through their bodies.

চলে ঘরে হৈতে কত উঠে চিতে গৌর-বিধু-অঙ্গ-সৌরভে মাতি ।
অথির অন্তর ভাবে গর গর আঁখি কোণে ভঙ্গী কত না ভাঁতি ॥

cale ghare haite kata uṭhe cite gaura-bidhu-aṅga-saurabhe māti |
athira antara bhābe gara gara ām̐khi koṇe bhaṅgī kata nā bhām̐ti ||

cale ghare haite — they come out of their houses; kata uṭhe cite — how much rises in the heart; gaura-bidhu-aṅga-saurabhe māti — intoxicated by the fragrance of the Gaura-moon's body; athira antara — the heart unsteady; bhābe gara gara — brimming with feeling; ām̐khi koṇe — from the corners of the eyes; bhaṅgī kata nā bhām̐ti — how many kinds of glances

2.2They come out of their houses — how many feelings rise in their hearts! — intoxicated by the fragrance of the body of the Gaura-moon; their hearts know no rest, brimming with feeling; from the corners of their eyes — how many different glances!

পরস্পর কত কহে অবেকত কে না নিছে তনু রঙ্গিণী রীতে ।
বাসভূষা বেশে ধৈরজ বিনাশে কে পারে সে শোভা উপমা দিতে ॥

paraspara kata kahe abekata ke nā niche tanu raṅgiṇī rīte |
bāsabhūṣā beśe dhairaja bināśe ke pāre se śobhā upamā dite ||

paraspara kata kahe — how much they say to one another; abekata — of the unmanifest (what cannot be told); ke nā niche tanu — who does not offer herself [for Him] (nichhani); raṅgiṇī rīte — playfully (lit. "in the manner of a playful woman"); bāsa-bhūṣā beśe — with dress, ornaments and attire; dhairaja bināśe — they destroy composure; ke pāre se śobhā upamā dite — who can compare that beauty

2.3How much they say to one another of what cannot be told! Which of them, playful, does not offer herself for Him? With their dress, ornaments and attire they shatter all composure — who could find a likeness for that beauty?

নূপুর কিঙ্কিণী নানা বাদ্যধ্বনি কি মধুর কহি না আসে মুখে ।
পানিসায়ি শেষে ভবনে প্রবেশে নরহরি হিয়া উথলে সুখে ॥

nūpura kiṅkiṇī nānā bādyadhvani ki madhura kahi nā āse mukhe |
pānisāyi śeṣe bhabane prabeśe narahari hiyā uthale sukhe ||

nūpura kiṅkiṇī — anklets and girdles of bells; nānā bādya-dhvani — the sound of many instruments; ki madhura — how sweet; kahi nā āse mukhe — words cannot tell; pāni-sāyi śeṣe — at the end of the water rite; bhabane prabeśe — they enter the house; narahari hiyā uthale sukhe — Narahari's heart overflows with joy

2.4Anklets, girdles of bells, the sounds of many instruments — how sweet, words cannot tell! Having completed the water rite, they enter the house — and Narahari's heart overflows with joy.5

vv. 1283–1286). Variant: 2.1 GPT1 "pāni-sahibāre", BR "pāni sāibāre" — "to perform the water rite" (translated by the sense of both readings). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. "Pani-sai" (jala sādhā) is a wedding custom: married women go with music to the Ganga and draw water for the bath of the bridegroom (or bride). of Gaura. We translate faithfully to the author; but the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati) does not accept the worship of Gaura in the mood of "Gaura-nagari": Gaura is Krishna Himself in the mood and lustre of Radha; He came to taste Her love, not to enjoy as a nagara. The Lord's attractiveness for the people of Navadvipa is the quality of Bhagavan, who attracts all; it is not worldly passion. The same holds for the other padas of the chapter about the women of Nadia (cf. note 39 of chapter 20).

3. Narahari — "kibā śrīśacī-bhabana mājhe…" (GPT1 p. 85, no. 18; BR)

The wedding bath of the bridegroom: amid auspicious cries the women loosen His locks and braid them again, oiling them, rub Him with turmeric and perfumes; He is bathed with Ganga water, and the poet playfully dries Him with a towel. Raga kamoda. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the BR.6

কিবা শ্রীশচী-ভবন মাঝে । বিবিধ মঙ্গল কলরবে সবে ভ্রময়ে বিবাহ কাজে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

kibā śrīśacī-bhabana mājhe | bibidha maṅgala kalarabe sabe bhramaye bibāha kāje || dhru ||

kibā — what [bustle]; śrī-śacī-bhabana mājhe — in the house of Sri Shachi; bibidha maṅgala kalarabe — amid manifold auspicious cries; sabe bhramaye — all move about; bibāha kāje — on the wedding tasks

3.1What [bustle] in the house of Sri Shachi! Amid manifold auspicious cries all are busy with the wedding tasks.

সে যে গোরা গোকুলের ইন্দু । বিবাহ-বিহিত স্নানে অতিশয় উথলে আনন্দ-সিন্ধু ॥

se ye gorā gokulera indu | bibāha-bihita snāne atiśaya uthale ānanda-sindhu ||

se ye gorā — for Gora; gokulera indu — is the Moon of Gokula; bibāha-bihita snāne — at the bath enjoined for the wedding; atiśaya — beyond measure; uthale ānanda-sindhu — the ocean of joy surges

3.2For Gora is the Moon of Gokula: at the bath enjoined before the wedding the ocean of joy surges beyond measure.

কুলবধূ সুমধুর ছাঁদে । সুচারু কুন্তলে তৈল দিব বলে বারে বারে আউলাঞা বাঁধে ॥

kulabadhū sumadhura chām̐de | sucāru kuntale taila diba bale bāre bāre āulāñā bām̐dhe ||

kulabadhū — the wives of noble families; sumadhura chām̐de — sweetly and gracefully; sucāru kuntale — into the lovely locks; taila diba bale — saying "let us put in oil"; bāre bāre — again and again; āulāñā bām̐dhe — loosen and braid them

3.3The wives of noble families, sweetly and gracefully, saying, "Let us oil His lovely locks," loosen and braid them again and again.

কেহ হলদি মাখায় গায় । হলদি মলিন হেরি হাসে সবে পরাণ নিছয়ে তায় ॥

keha haladi mākhāya gāya | haladi malina heri hāse sabe parāṇa nichaye tāya ||

keha haladi mākhāya gāya — one rubs [His] body with turmeric; haladi malina heri — seeing the turmeric grow dim; hāse sabe — all laugh; parāṇa nichaye tāya — they give their lives for Him (the nimchhani rite)

3.4One rubs His body with turmeric; seeing the turmeric grow dim, all laugh and give their lives for Him.7

কেহ গন্ধদ্রব্য দেই অঙ্গে । সে না অঙ্গ-গন্ধে গন্ধমদ হরে উপমা দিব কি সঙ্গে ॥

keha gandhadrabya dei aṅge | se nā aṅga-gandhe gandhamada hare upamā diba ki saṅge ||

keha gandha-drabya dei aṅge — one puts perfumes on His body; se nā aṅga-gandhe — the fragrance of that body; gandha-mada hare — takes away the pride of perfumes; upamā diba ki saṅge — with what shall I compare it

3.5One anoints His body with perfumes — but the fragrance of that body robs the perfumes of their pride: with what to compare it?

অভিষেক কৈল গঙ্গাজলে । নরহরি পানি-তোলা লইয়া তনু পোছয়ে কৌতুক ছলে ॥

abhiṣeka kaila gaṅgājale | narahari pāni-tolā laiyā tanu pochaye kautuka chale ||

abhiṣeka kaila gaṅgājale — they bathed [Him] with Ganga water; narahari — Narahari; pāni-tolā laiyā — taking a towel; tanu pochaye — dries the body; kautuka chale — as if in play

3.6They bathed Him with Ganga water; Narahari, taking a towel, dries His body as if in play.

vv. 1287–1292). Variants: 3.2 GPT1 "sthāne" ("in the place"), BR "snāne" ("at the bath") — following the BR; 3.5 GPT1 "upamā diba ki saṅge", BR-1912 "ke dibe upamā aṅge". Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Line 3.1 is the refrain (dhru). waves something (in poetry — one's very life) around the beloved to ward off misfortune. The playful care of the women who perform the wedding rites (anointing the bridegroom with turmeric and oil) is festive merriment, not nagari-bhava.

4. Narahari — "āju kata nā ānanda mane…" (GPT1 p. 86, no. 19; BR)

His friends dress the bridegroom: they anoint Him with sandal, draw the tilaka, adorn His curls with a garland of malati, put on earrings, necklace, bracelets and rings and a golden chain on His waist; the poet, having clothed Him in a red-bordered cloth, beholds His beauty. Raga kamoda. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the BR.8

আজু কত না আনন্দ মনে । বসিয়া আসনে বিশ্বম্ভর-বেশ রচয়ে বয়স্যগণে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

āju kata nā ānanda mane | basiyā āsane biśvambhara-beśa racaye bayasyagaṇe || dhru ||

āju kata nā ānanda mane — how much joy in the heart today; basiyā āsane — seated on a seat; biśvambhara-beśa — Vishvambhara's attire; racaye bayasya-gaṇe — His friends arrange

4.1How much joy in the heart today! Seating Vishvambhara on a seat, His friends dress Him.

গন্ধ চন্দন চরচে গায় । বিরচয়ে চারু ললাটে তিলক কেবা না ভুলয় তায় ॥

gandha candana carace gāya | biracaye cāru lalāṭe tilaka kebā nā bhulaya tāya ||

gandha candana — fragrant sandal paste; carace gāya — they smear on the body; biracaye cāru lalāṭe tilaka — they draw a lovely tilaka on the forehead; kebā nā bhulaya tāya — whom would it not enchant

4.2They anoint His body with fragrant sandal paste and draw a lovely tilaka on His forehead — whom would it not enchant?

বাঁধি চাঁচর চিকুর ভালে । মনের উল্লাসে মধুর ছাঁদে বেড়য়ে মালতী মালে ॥

bām̐dhi cām̐cara cikura bhāle | manera ullāse madhura chām̐de beṛaye mālatī māle ||

bām̐dhi cām̐cara cikura bhāle — gathering the curling locks on the brow; manera ullāse — in gladness of heart; madhura chām̐de — sweetly and gracefully; beṛaye mālatī māle — they wind them with a garland of malati

4.3Gathering the curling locks above His brow, in gladness of heart, sweetly and gracefully they wind them with a garland of malati.

কাণে কুণ্ডল অর্পণ করে । ঝলকয়ে গণ্ডতটে গণ্ডযুগ দর্পণ দরপ হরে ॥

kāṇe kuṇḍala arpaṇa kare | jhalakaye gaṇḍataṭe gaṇḍayuga darpaṇa darapa hare ||

kāṇe kuṇḍala arpaṇa kare — they put earrings in His ears; jhalakaye gaṇḍa-taṭe — they flash by the cheeks; gaṇḍa-yuga — the two cheeks; darpaṇa darapa hare — rob mirrors of their pride

4.4They put earrings in His ears — they flash beside His cheeks, and His cheeks rob mirrors of their pride.

গলে দেই মণিময় হার । পরিসর বুকে দোলে সুললিত কে দিবে উপমা তার ॥

gale dei maṇimaya hāra | parisara buke dole sulalita ke dibe upamā tāra ||

gale dei maṇimaya hāra — they put a jewelled necklace on His neck; parisara buke — on the broad chest; dole sulalita — it sways charmingly; ke dibe upamā tāra — who will find its likeness

4.5They put a necklace of jewels on His neck; it sways charmingly on His broad chest — who can find a likeness for it?

বাহু অঙ্গদ বলয়া করে । অঙ্গুলে অঙ্গুরি সোঁপি মুখপানে চাহি না ধৈরজ ধরে ॥

bāhu aṅgada balayā kare | aṅgule aṅguri som̐pi mukhapāne cāhi nā dhairaja dhare ||

bāhu aṅgada — armlets on the arms; balayā kare — bracelets on the hands; aṅgule aṅguri som̐pi — putting rings on the fingers; mukha-pāne cāhi — looking at the face; nā dhairaja dhare — they cannot keep composure

4.6On His arms armlets and bracelets, on His fingers they put rings — and, looking at His face, they cannot keep their composure.

সিংহ জিনি মাজাখানি ক্ষীণ । সোণার শিকলি সাজাইতে আঁখি হইল নিমিষহীন ॥

siṃha jini mājākhāni kṣīṇa | soṇāra śikali sājāite ām̐khi haila nimiṣahīna ||

siṃha jini — surpassing a lion's; mājākhāni kṣīṇa — the waist is slender; soṇāra śikali sājāite — adorning it with a golden chain; ām̐khi haila nimiṣa-hīna — the eyes became unblinking

4.7His waist is slender, slenderer than a lion's; as they adorn it with a golden chain, their eyes cease to blink.
